examples.question_text:
(a) A shop sells $3$ kg of rice for $\$8.40$. Find the cost of $5$ kg.
(b) A machine processes $450$ labels in $3$ minutes. How long does it take to process $1650$ labels at the same rate?
examples.solution_text:
(a) Write equivalent rates: $\frac{\$8.40}{3\text{ kg}}=\frac{\$x}{5\text{ kg}}$.
Multiply both sides by $5$: $x=\frac{8.40}{3}\times5=14$. The cost is $\$14$.
(b) $\frac{450\text{ labels}}{3\text{ min}}=\frac{1650\text{ labels}}{x\text{ min}}$.
Take the reciprocal of both sides: $\frac{3\text{ min}}{450\text{ labels}}=\frac{x\text{ min}}{1650\text{ labels}}$.
Multiply both sides by $1650$: $x=\frac3{450}\times1650=11$ minutes.

examples.question_text:
A car uses $8$ L of fuel per $100$ km.
(a) How much fuel is needed for $175$ km?
(b) How far can it travel on $36$ L?
examples.solution_text:
(a) $\frac{8\text{ L}}{100\text{ km}}=\frac{x\text{ L}}{175\text{ km}}$.
$x=\frac8{100}\times175=14$ L.
(b) $\frac{8\text{ L}}{100\text{ km}}=\frac{36\text{ L}}{x\text{ km}}$.
Take reciprocals: $\frac{100\text{ km}}{8\text{ L}}=\frac{x\text{ km}}{36\text{ L}}$.
$x=\frac{100}{8}\times36=450$ km. Keep litres and kilometres in matching positions.

examples.question_text: The water in a tank falls from $84\,000$ L to $54\,000$ L over $4$ days. At the same rate, how many more days will it take to empty?
examples.solution_text:
Water lost $=84\,000-54\,000=30\,000$ L.
Rate $=30\,000\div4=7500$ L/day.
$\frac{7500\text{ L}}{1\text{ day}}=\frac{54\,000\text{ L}}{x\text{ days}}$.
Take reciprocals: $\frac{1\text{ day}}{7500\text{ L}}=\frac{x\text{ days}}{54\,000\text{ L}}$.
$x=54\,000\div7500=7.2$ more days. Use the water lost to find the rate, then the water remaining to find the extra time.

examples.question_text:
(a) Paint covers $10$ m$^2$ per litre. How much paint is needed for two coats on a wall $2.4$ m by $3.5$ m?
(b) Fertiliser is spread at $0.15$ kg/m$^2$. How many whole $15$ kg bags must be bought for $240$ m$^2$?
examples.solution_text:
(a) Total area to paint $=2.4\times3.5\times2=16.8$ m$^2$.
$\frac{10\text{ m}^2}{1\text{ L}}=\frac{16.8\text{ m}^2}{x\text{ L}}$.
Take reciprocals and solve: $x=16.8\div10=1.68$ L.
(b) $\frac{0.15\text{ kg}}{1\text{ m}^2}=\frac{x\text{ kg}}{240\text{ m}^2}$ gives $x=0.15\times240=36$ kg.
$36\div15=2.4$ bags, so buy $3$ whole bags to have enough.

examples.question_text: A camping group uses $22$ L of water every $5$ days. It carries $70$ L. Will the water last a $17$ day trip at the same rate?
examples.solution_text:
$\frac{22\text{ L}}{5\text{ days}}=\frac{x\text{ L}}{17\text{ days}}$.
$x=\frac{22}{5}\times17=74.8$ L.
No. The trip needs $74.8$ L, which is more than the $70$ L carried.

examples.question_text: The exchange rate is $0.80$ US dollars per Australian dollar. How many Australian dollars does Amira receive for US$\$632$?
examples.solution_text:
$\begin{align*}\frac{0.80\text{ US}}{1\text{ A}}&=\frac{632\text{ US}}{x\text{ A}}\end{align*}$
Take the reciprocal of both sides.
$\begin{align*}\frac{1\text{ A}}{0.80\text{ US}}&=\frac{x\text{ A}}{632\text{ US}}\\x&=\frac{632}{0.80}\\x&=790\end{align*}$
She receives A$\$790$.

examples.question_text: A recipe uses $360$ g of flour and $120$ mL of milk. A cook uses $540$ g of flour and says, “I added $180$ g, so I should also add $180$ mL and use $300$ mL of milk.” Explain the error and find the correct amount of milk.
examples.solution_text:
The same amount cannot be added to quantities with different units. Keep the flour-to-milk rate unchanged.
$\frac{360\text{ g}}{120\text{ mL}}=\frac{540\text{ g}}{x\text{ mL}}$.
Take reciprocals: $\frac{120\text{ mL}}{360\text{ g}}=\frac{x\text{ mL}}{540\text{ g}}$.
$x=\frac{120}{360}\times540=180$ mL.
The flour was multiplied by $1.5$, so the milk must also be multiplied by $1.5$, rather than increased by $180$ mL.

examples.question_text: A factory produces $35$ bottles per minute. How many bottles can it produce in $6$ hours?
examples.solution_text:
$6\text{ h}=360\text{ min}$.
$\begin{align*}\frac{35\text{ bottles}}{1\text{ min}}&=\frac{x\text{ bottles}}{360\text{ min}}\\x&=35\times360\\x&=12\,600\end{align*}$
The factory produces $12\,600$ bottles.

examples.question_text: One litre of a drink contains $80$ g of sugar. How many millilitres of the drink contain $6$ g of sugar?
examples.solution_text:
$1\text{ L}=1000\text{ mL}$.
$\frac{80\text{ g}}{1000\text{ mL}}=\frac{6\text{ g}}{x\text{ mL}}$.
Take the reciprocal of both sides.
$\begin{align*}\frac{1000\text{ mL}}{80\text{ g}}&=\frac{x\text{ mL}}{6\text{ g}}\\x&=\frac{1000}{80}\times6\\x&=75\end{align*}$
The drink contains $6$ g of sugar in $75$ mL.

examples.question_text: Leah earns $\$24$ per hour. She works $18$ hours in week $1$ and $22$ hours in week $2$. How many more hours must she work to earn $\$1500$?
examples.solution_text:
Earned so far: $(18+22)\times\$24=\$960$.
Still needed: $\$1500-\$960=\$540$.
$\frac{\$24}{1\text{ h}}=\frac{\$540}{x\text{ h}}$.
Take the reciprocal of both sides.
$\begin{align*}\frac{1\text{ h}}{\$24}&=\frac{x\text{ h}}{\$540}\\x&=\frac{540}{24}\\x&=22.5\end{align*}$
She needs to work $22.5$ more hours.

coverage.summary: Retained six examples exactly, repaired the unsupported chained currency example and added three examples covering time conversion, volume conversion and additional earnings. All ten examples have separate editable question and solution fields and source-supported methods. Solution prose and mathematics inherit renderer blue without colour wrappers. No examples require diagrams or phantom equals gutters. Assessment locators were classified only; practice and quiz mathematics were neither changed nor re-audited. Final rendering and label-size checks remain with the later capture stage.

examples.derivation: Source question 20(b–c) supports one-way conversion using reciprocal equivalent rates. Australian dollars = 632 ÷ 0.80 = 790, so Amira receives A$790.
Source question 5 supports converting hours to minutes before applying production rates. 6 × 60 = 360 minutes; 35 × 360 = 12,600 bottles.
Source question 15 supports litre-to-millilitre conversion followed by reciprocal equivalent rates. 1 L = 1000 mL; required volume = 1000 × 6 ÷ 80 = 75 mL.
Source question 14(c) supports finding existing earnings, subtracting from the target and calculating additional hours. (18 + 22) × 24 = $960; $1500 − $960 = $540; 540 ÷ 24 = 22.5 additional hours.

review.summary: All 26 exact assessment locators are mapped, and all distinct assessed methods have example coverage. Retained examples have no genuine gutter, diagram or annotation defects. All examples separate questions from solutions, use supported single-dollar mathematics and inherit blue solution prose/math without colour wrappers. No source exception or diagram is required. Practice and quiz mathematics were not re-audited. Final rendering verification remains with the later capture stage.
